_readme: Forty realistic decide() calls used as the eval set by scripts/test-eval-situations.mjs. Unlike the 20 situations this file replaced (2026-09-06 and earlier), this `expected` was NOT drafted by running decide() against the catalog and reading off the winner -- it's a cold answer key, built independently by a separate pass with real, cited, per-task usage/vote/vendor-guidance/enterprise-case-study signals (see each situation's `signals[]`) and no visibility into this engine's internals, specifically so this eval can't grade its own homework. `start_here_any_of` and `acceptable` are both 'any of these would be a fine top pick' -- acceptable is the broader set; a real engine only needs to land in start_here_any_of to pass. `must_not_start` bars a model from the #1 spot only (it may still appear lower in the shortlist); `must_not_include` bars it from the shortlist entirely -- reserved for a hard, structural exclusion (a China-hosted vendor under noChinaHosted, or a preview/beta SKU under an enterprise-style input), never just 'this one is not the best fit'. `input.have` and `input.dataRule` are stored in decide()'s own array/object shape (openrouter-anything -> ['any'], claude-only -> ['anthropic'], etc. -- see convert_situations.py in the PR that added this file for the exact mapping and how it was checked against the key's own reachable-count derivation text). `input.enterprise` is passed straight into decide() as an explicit override of its own have/volume/dataRule heuristic (assets/decide.mjs's isEnterpriseInput) -- the key's authors already know the situation's own context, so there's no reason to re-derive it. See data/eval/must-never.json for the companion set of absolute per-(task,stance) and per-context rules this same key ships.
